items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: And when they asked me to play, Noah Evans who was in charge of recruiting people, and Steve Shaffer. Is it Steve? [INTERVIEWER] Paul Shaffer.

ctx.x: Hey that’s okay. Thelonious Monk didn’t have the greatest hand technique, right?

But getting back to Lew. I was a slow arranger so a couple, I’m not going to mention any people, but I did maybe one-third of the charts. Dick was very quick. And three or four of the charts like I couldn’t finish. I got very emotional because I didn’t have a technique like Dick was talking about you know. He had to write for strings for the week. His assignment, or a choral thing, you know, voices. And I didn’t have to do that at Berklee, maybe once or twice so I didn’t get over that. So I was very slow usually.…

going to perform. I thought it’d be an ego trip, I’m the one guy coming from Boston down to the New York area, everybody else, there’s about fifteen musicians, Wynton Marsalis played also. But most people came from New York. And when they asked me to play, Noah Evans who was in charge of recruiting people, and Steve Shaffer. Is it Steve?
